sections.html:
Millcreek Township wraps the lakefront and suburban ground west and south of the city of Erie. The 2020 count was 54,070, which makes it the biggest township in western Pennsylvania, and the July 2025 estimate is 52,680. Most land is given over to retail, services, light industry, schools and residential streets, so a house here is nearly always a suburban lot on public roads and utilities.

About two of every three homes are owner-occupied. Much of the housing went up in the postwar boom, when population climbed from 16,776 in 1950 to 36,946 in 1970, so the roof, furnace and wiring in a typical Millcreek house are decades old and buyers price that in. Because 23.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, long-owned homes and estates make up part of what reaches the market.

Millcreek's Bureau of Code Enforcement applies the International Property Maintenance Code and the International Fire Code, so an unresolved violation on your parcel can hold up a closing. A neighbor's complaint or a phone call usually opens a case.

The office deals with problems such as these:

  • Weeds, debris and trash piling up on the lot
  • Sidewalks that are a tripping hazard, and unshoveled snow or ice on sidewalks
  • Electrical, building and fire violations
  • Pest infestations and abandoned vehicles on private property
  • Illegal burning, demolition permits and condemnations

A notice of violation gives you 20 days to appeal the inspector's decision. If you let it sit, the inspector comes back for a second look and can file a non-traffic summary citation with the local magistrate, who then schedules a hearing for the owner of record. Vacant houses follow the same path, and when compliance never arrives the township can move to clean and secure the building or raze it.

If your house is empty or run down, clear these items before you list, or write down what remains and share that list with the buyer before you sign a contract.

Millcreek calls Airbnb or VRBO style stays Limited Lodging: renting to the same guest for at least two and no more than 30 consecutive nights. A stay beyond 30 nights is a long-term rental and falls outside the rule. Limited Lodging is allowed only in certain zones, and only after the property registers with the Code Enforcement Office.

The allowed areas are the MU-1 Neighborhood Mixed Use, MU-2 Corridor Mixed Use and PI Presque Isle Gateway districts, plus two Limited Lodging Overlay areas near the lake. One overlay runs from the west line of the Hartt Estates Subdivision along Montpelier Avenue, south to West Lake Road and north to Lake Erie. The other starts at the east line of Calvary Cemetery and runs to West 11th Street, the Corridor Mixed Use 2 boundary and the Presque Isle district.

A buyer who wants a lakeside house for guest stays should phone the Zoning Office at 814-833-2935 and ask whether the parcel sits inside one of those areas. If you have been renting the house this way yourself, hand the registration paperwork to the buyer.

Erie County, not the township, sets your assessed value. The Board of Assessment Appeals takes the annual appeal form between January 1 and August 1 and holds hearings from July to October. Filing costs $50 for a parcel, with $10 more for each added parcel in the same property.

What the appeal form asks of you:

  • An owner may speak at the hearing, or a Pennsylvania attorney may; a company owner must use an attorney.
  • Name up to three comparables, either recent sales or active listings.
  • Send two copies of your evidence ten days ahead, and make sure any appraisal is effective within six months of the appeal.
  • An appeal reopens the valuation, so the figure can fall, hold or rise.

The county's assessment office also has forms for the homestead exclusion, owner changes, Clean and Green land and catastrophic loss, and it publishes a millage chart each year. Look up Millcreek Township and its school district on that chart to see the rates behind a bill.

Deeds for Millcreek houses are recorded at the Erie County Recorder of Deeds in the courthouse on West Sixth Street. That office also collects the state and local transfer tax and the county's recording fees. Deeds between spouses, parents and children, or siblings can be exempt. The county's tax sale material quotes 2 percent as the standard transfer cost, so ask the Recorder how the local split works on an ordinary Millcreek sale.

Pennsylvania's seller disclosure law, Title 68 Chapter 73, has you fill out a statement and hand the buyer a signed copy before any agreement of transfer is signed. It covers the roof, basement, drainage and flood risk indicators. An executor or other fiduciary selling for an estate is excused from it, which applies to inherited Millcreek homes.

Act 74 of 2026 adds a written flood insurance warning to the seller package once the Insurance Department puts up its flood page. That matters most for parcels near the lake.

sections.h2: What if property taxes are behind?
sections.html:
The county's annual upset sale covers parcels with taxes two or more years behind, and it runs as an online auction. A winning bid does not end the owner's rights until the bidder pays in full, so you can still clear the debt first and keep the house. After full payment, nothing can be redeemed.

Parcels that do not sell go to a judicial sale and then a repository list, and the owner cannot bid on a parcel in either group. The buyer inherits liens and judgments and receives a quit claim deed. A sale before this point usually keeps more of your equity. Call the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff figure and to learn where your parcel stands.

sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in Millcreek?
sections.html:
The right route depends on repairs, timing and any code problems at the property.

  • Agent listing: a fit when the house shows well and you can wait through showings, a buyer's inspection and loan approval.
  • Owner sale: skips the agent but puts pricing, the disclosure form and negotiation on you.
  • Cash sale as is: used for estate homes, houses with open Millcreek code notices, tenant-occupied properties and places needing work, generally at less than a repaired house would bring.

Whichever way you go, start with the same three chores. Pull the Erie County parcel record, confirm that no township notice is open, and complete the state disclosure statement. A cash sale skips the showings, the buyer's lender and the repair requests, so it can close faster, but compare the offer against what a repaired listing would net after repairs and fees.

faqs.q: Is Millcreek a city or a township?
faqs.a: Millcreek is a township in Erie County. The city of Erie annexed pieces of it over the years, but the township keeps its own zoning, code enforcement and police.

faqs.q: Can a Millcreek house with open code violations still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. A notice of violation leaves 20 days to appeal, and ignored notices can reach the local magistrate as a summary citation. Tell buyers about the notice and ask the Code Enforcement office what closes the file.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Millcreek assessment?
faqs.a: Erie County takes the appeal form from January 1 through August 1, and hearings run July through October. Filing costs $50 a parcel, and an appeal can raise the value as well as lower it.

faqs.q: Must Millcreek sellers hand buyers a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Pennsylvania requires a signed property disclosure statement before an agreement of transfer is signed, except for fiduciaries selling for an estate.

faqs.q: Can I run my Millcreek house as an Airbnb before selling?
faqs.a: Only inside the zones where the township allows Limited Lodging, meaning guest stays of 2 to 30 nights. Those are the MU-1, MU-2 and Presque Isle Gateway districts and two overlay areas, and registration with Code Enforcement is required.
